question: The resolving power of the eye is 1 minute of arc. What is the cor-responding dimension on the retina?
model_outputs:
The resolving power of the eye is 1 minute of arc, which is 1/60 of a degree. We need to convert this to radians. 1 degree = pi/180 radians, so 1 minute of arc = (pi/180)/60 radians. The angular resolution, $\theta$, is related to the dimension, $d$, and the distance, $f$, by $d = f \theta$. Here, $f$ is the focal length of the eye, which is about 2 cm or 20 mm.  So, $d = 20 \text{ mm} \times (\frac{\pi}{180} \times \frac{1}{60}) = 20 \times \frac{\pi}{10800} \approx 20 \times \frac{3.14}{10800} \approx \frac{62.8}{10800} \approx 0.0058 \text{ mm} \approx 5 \text{ microns}$.

The answer is (I).
